I wrote the harness to `/tmp/locus-SND001/repo/__locus_harness_dim_2.c`. I haven't run it through KLEE, so I don't know yet whether it finds a counterexample.

- **Data flow:** `paf_read_header` reads `marker`. If it is `PAF_MARKER` or `FAP_MARKER`, the code reads `version`, `endianness`, `samplerate`, `format`, `channels` and `source` from the header. Any other marker returns `SFE_PAF_NO_MARKER`.
- **Path constraint:** The code between the predicate and the canary calls `_exit(1)` unless `version == 0`. The harness therefore assumes `version == 0`. I added this constraint myself because it is on the path, and the task pattern didn't list it.
- **Canary:** The canary line fires when `channels < 1` or `channels > SF_MAX_CHANNELS`. The harness asserts the opposite. `channels` is unconstrained, so KLEE should be able to violate the assertion.
- **Assumption on the predicate:** The harness assumes `!(marker != PAF_MARKER && marker != FAP_MARKER)`, so `marker` is one of the two valid markers.

- **Constants:** The harness defines `SF_MAX_CHANNELS` as 1024 from memory of libsndfile and did not check it against the repo headers. I also defined `MAKE_MARKER` as the little-endian byte order without reading `sfendian.h`. The marker byte order doesn't change the result, because `channels` is independent of it. A wrong `SF_MAX_CHANNELS` would change which `channels` values count as out of range.
